text: The mapping version label and the valid-from and valid-to dates are held on the role rows of the environment in `rwb_access` and added by this key's migration; no new table is created for the mapping, and an applied version is never edited.
why: `role` carries no version or date column in TSD P4 v3 T3.1 while legacy AC3 needs a new mapping version with a valid from date, and the ownership map gives P4 no further table for a mapping.
read: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-039); legacy RWB-AD-001 AC3 and Data table; ownership map (`role` is P4's); DP-15.
confirm: The tech lead of rwb-access and the data steward
impact: The mapping is versioned on the role rows; a second version carries the rows of that version and closes the earlier valid-to, and no other service is affected.

text: The Workbench mapping is `role.entra_group` (DF-REF-039) of the environment's role rows, and the ACE view `v_ace_iam_group` is a read-only reference of the group, its source system and its data-as-of date; the view's `role_code` is never the Workbench mapping and is never read as the authority.
why: R-PREC puts the technical specification above the functional specification: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 defines `entra_group` as a Workbench column with source Entra ID, while the FSD field catalog calls the group a view column and not a Workbench column.
read: TSD P4 v3 T3.1; FSD P4 v3 A2.1 and A2.3 field catalog; R-PREC rule 6 over rule 7; DP-05; legacy RWB-E1-022 section 2.
confirm: The solution architect and the bank IAM integration lead
impact: The mapping is maintainable as data; the view is read only for the group list and its freshness, so a change in the bank IAM's view never silently changes a role.

text: The environment code of a deployment is read as a parameter through the parameters contract of rwb-case (DP-06), so one build serves every environment; the parameter code and the codes beyond SIT are fixed when the parameter catalogue is published.
why: The legacy story maps a group to one role in each environment and no source names the environment value or the parameter that carries it, while no business value may be written in code.
read: Legacy RWB-AD-001 story statement and AC1; TSD P4 v3 T3.1; DP-06; FSD P4 v3 A1.1 constraints.
confirm: The tech lead of rwb-access and the parameters owner of rwb-case
impact: A new environment is a parameter row, not a build; a wrong parameter refuses the change with MSG-GEN-001 rather than writing a mapping in the wrong environment.

text: The mapping is read, changed and read by version through three operations on `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin`, with Platform administration R for the two reads and C for the change, idempotent by Idempotency-Key on the change, and with no in-place update operation.
why: No source names the operations of the mapping: the ownership map and TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A carry only GET /admin/roles (API-P4-007), and the legacy endpoint table names rule-version paths that belong to another story.
read: Ownership map (GET /admin/roles is P4's); TSD P4 v3 API-P4-007 and T6.1; legacy RWB-AD-001 Endpoints and Permission checks; Template and Rules §R4.
confirm: The solution architect and the security administrator
impact: The three paths are this key's contract; a later change is an additive change within major version 1 and a breaking change is a new major version.

text: A mapping change is published as `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` on `rwb.access.events.v1` with change kind MAPPING; no dedicated mapping event is added, because a mapping change is an access-policy change and the only consumer of the mapping is the sign-in of rwb-access.
why: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 43 give `rwb-access` exactly two event names and slide 20 shows the estate refreshing cached permission data on AccessPolicyChanged, so a second name would add a contract without a consumer.
read: Architecture v5 slides 14, 20, 43 and 44; DP-14 naming; TSD P4 v3 T5.3 (events: none).
confirm: The solution architect and the event platform owner
impact: One event name and one consumer signal; the change kind is added inside the existing payload version, and no consumer subscribes to a name that does not exist.

text: A mapping version needs no second approval: the security administrator writes it under the C letter, and the decision-record entry names the actor, the version and the time.
why: The legacy story names the security administrator as the actor and no approver, and it does not put the mapping on the reference-load approval path of the module.
read: Legacy RWB-AD-001 Story, Permission checks and Test cases; TSD P4 v3 T6.1; FSD P4 v3 A2.3.
confirm: The security administrator and internal audit
impact: The change is one recorded write; if a second approval is later required it is a new operation on the reference-load path of rwb-case and a new story.

text: Every mapping change and every refusal is written as a local decision-record entry through the library of DP-03 and published on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; the central ledger and its query stay P7 rwb-decision's.
why: DP-03 is how this service records a decision, and the architecture gives every service its own local record with the central ledger to P7, so the access log of the mapping is one chain with the decisions of the service.
read: Architecture v5 slides 20, 28 and 41; DP-03; TSD P4 v3 T6.3; FSD P4 v3 A2.3.
impact: The access log of the mapping is this service's chain; a cross-estate query needs the P7 query API and is the integration story's.

text: At sign-in the mapping version in force on that day resolves to the person's roles and stays with the session until it ends; a group with no mapping, or a mapping to an inactive role, gives no role and the person sees MSG-P4-001, and the refusal is recorded.
why: The matrix and masking versions of this run resolve at sign-in and stay until the session ends, and the legacy criteria AC2 and AC3 require the version in force at the session and a refusal for an unmapped group.
read: Legacy RWB-AD-001 AC2 and AC3; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-001-04; legacy RWB-E1-022 sections 2 and 4; template defaults of this run.
confirm: The security administrator and the owner of RWB-P4-E1022
impact: A mapping change reaches a person at their next sign-in, and an open session is never re-resolved mid-session.
